The exact-model QSC manual states that "audio power" is connected to the loudspeaker and that it has no crossover network or internal processing; the only inputs are NL8 audio-power connectors. This is an explicit statement of the external-amplification signal path, so the stored passive value is retained and re-sourced from the specification sheet to the manual.

Neither the specification sheet nor the user manual states passive/active or built-in amplification for the WL212-sw; the manual only describes the NL8/NL4 wiring to the transducers and a 1100 W continuous power-handling capability. Under the standing explicit-evidence rule the Round 22 manufacturer-verified promotion is retracted and the field returns to unknown.

entries.note: Round 27 (2026-10-19): the 20 kHz self-conflict is resolved. The same manual's LSR32 Amplitude & Phase table reads 92 dB at 20 kHz and the LSR32 Acoustic Contribution fundamental table also reads 92 dB at 20 kHz. The 61 dB value belongs to the LSR28P section (Amplitude and Phase, 61 dB at 10 kHz with a blank 20 kHz row), not to the LSR32. The stored 27-row series was also not the LSR32 table: 12 of its 27 values differed (30, 40, 50, 70, 80, 300, 400, 500, 600, 700, 900, 1000 Hz) and it omitted the 20 kHz row. It has been replaced by the verbatim 28-row table; the superseded rows are preserved in this resolution record and in scripts/research/round27-value-history.json.

Two official editions of the same sheet disagree with each other and with both stored series. The FR edition has 86 rows (2400 and 2600 Hz, no 2500 Hz); the EN edition has 87 rows (2400, 2500, 2600 Hz) and 64 of the shared sensitivity values differ. The FR impedance column falls to 1.1 ohm, below the 7.0 ohm minimum the same sheet publishes; the EN column peaks at 110 ohm at 2500 Hz. The stored 85-point series matches neither edition (9 values differ from FR, 61 from EN, and it has 2500 Hz without 2400/2600). Text-derived -3 dB and -10 dB crossings from either table do not reproduce the stated 77 Hz-16 kHz / 52 Hz-19 kHz limits, so the published limits cannot validate the tables either. Response data stays excluded from simulation; no series is adopted and no point is rewritten.
